name: Teton + Yellowstone + Oregon Cascades Multi-City Loop

dates.why: Aug 31-Sep 13 keeps the established late-summer/early-September planning window, gives Yellowstone and Crater Lake better weather odds, and leaves Oregon as the softer final act before flying home from Portland.

exchangeRateNote: Domestic trip; all planning numbers are USD and should be re-priced before booking.
positioning: The expanded Teton alternate: three nights in Jackson/Tetons, four nights across Yellowstone, then a flight hop to Oregon for Bend, Crater Lake, Mount Hood, and the Columbia Gorge.
routeLabel: ATL -> JAC -> Tetons -> Yellowstone -> PDX/RDM -> Bend -> Crater Lake -> Hood River -> PDX -> ATL
routeRationale: Start in Jackson so the highest-friction lodging and national-park pacing happen while energy is highest.
Use two Yellowstone bases, Old Faithful and Canyon, so geysers, Yellowstone Lake, Hayden Valley, and the canyon are not all forced from one hotel.
Fly from the northern Rockies to Oregon instead of driving the full intermountain distance with a one-year-old.
Use Bend/Sunriver as the practical Oregon laundry base, then add one Crater Lake lodge night and two Columbia Gorge/Mount Hood nights.
Keep the Oregon ending flexible: if Crater Lake weather or smoke is bad, pivot to Bend, Newberry, High Desert Museum, or Mount Hood without breaking the trip.

budget.note: Planning estimate for a complex domestic open-jaw trip. The biggest swing factors are Yellowstone lodging, the intra-west flight, Oregon car one-way/drop fees, and whether Crater Lake Lodge or Mazama cabins are available.

recommended.label: Recommended multi-city flight pattern

return.airline: Delta preferred if nonstop is available
return.duration: about 4.5-5 hours nonstop, longer with connection

recommended.infantNote: Domestic infant-in-lap should not require a separate fare, but add the infant to every ticketed segment, including the JAC/BOI/RDM/PDX positioning hop.
recommended.budgetNote: Use Google Flights multi-city search for ATL-JAC, JAC/BOI/RDM/PDX positioning, and PDX-ATL. If the JAC to Oregon hop is ugly, drive Yellowstone to Boise and fly BOI-PDX/RDM.

alternates.label: Reverse-route alternative
alternates.summary: ATL to PDX first, Oregon loop, fly PDX/RDM to JAC, finish with Tetons and return JAC to ATL. This can work if Yellowstone lodging is better later in the window.

alternates.label: Boise bridge alternative
alternates.summary: After Yellowstone, drive to Boise, overnight near BOI, and fly BOI to Portland or Redmond. More driving, but often simpler and cheaper than small-airport hops.

bases.name: Jackson / Teton arrival
bases.why: Walkable Jackson base for arrival, groceries, National Elk Refuge/Wildlife Art, and the first Grand Teton days.

bases.name: Old Faithful / West Thumb base
bases.why: Lets Yellowstone's geyser country be walkable in short boardwalk chunks instead of a day-trip slog.

bases.name: Canyon / Hayden Valley base
bases.why: Best practical center for Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, Hayden Valley wildlife, Norris, and lake/canyon backups.

bases.name: Oregon arrival / Bend practical base
bases.hotel: Sunriver Resort or SCP Redmond Hotel
bases.why: Laundry, kitchen, pool, and easy access to Bend, Smith Rock, Newberry, and the High Desert Museum.

bases.name: Crater Lake rim or Mazama
bases.hotel: Crater Lake Lodge or Mazama Village Cabin
bases.why: A one-night national-park lodge moment keeps the rim sunset/sunrise possible without making the baby sleep in a new place too often.

bases.name: Columbia Gorge / Mount Hood finale
bases.hotel: Skamania Lodge or Hood River Hotel
bases.room: View room or practical downtown room
bases.why: Waterfalls, Mount Hood, river views, and a manageable drive to PDX for the flight home.

dailyItinerary.title: Fly ATL to Jackson and reset
dailyItinerary.transport: Fly ATL to JAC on the best multi-city fare; pick up rental SUV only if arrival is not too late, otherwise shuttle/taxi and collect the car Day 2.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Arrival only: check in, grab groceries/snacks, and do a very short Town Square stroller loop if everyone is awake.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the flight arrives late, skip town and go straight to the room.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport breakfast/lunch, grocery snacks, simple Jackson dinner or takeout.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Protect bedtime after the westbound travel day; this trip is ambitious enough without a first-night outing.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Price ATL-JAC as part of a multi-city ticket with the Oregon hop and PDX-ATL return.
dailyItinerary.why: Jackson gives the trip an immediate mountain arrival and puts the hardest-to-book park section first, when everyone has the most patience.
moments: Land with the Tetons visible from the airport if the weather cooperates.
Set up groceries, diapers, and sleep gear before the park days.
Keep the first night deliberately boring.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Day 1 carries the full multi-city flight placeholder for two adults; re-price before booking.

dailyItinerary.title: Jackson wildlife art and town warm-up
dailyItinerary.transport: Local Jackson driving/walking; pick up rental SUV if not collected on arrival.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: National Museum of Wildlife Art, Elk Refuge road/pullouts, Town Square, and a slow lunch.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If everyone needs recovery, keep it to groceries, town stroller loop, and hotel downtime.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Hotel/grocery breakfast, Persephone-style cafe lunch, early casual dinner in Jackson.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Stroller works well today; this is the decompression day before park roads.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Reserve rental car with confirmed car seat or bring your own.
dailyItinerary.why: This day keeps the baby near services while still starting the wildlife and mountain mood.
moments: See wildlife art before chasing real wildlife from the car.
Use Jackson as a supply base.
Avoid a full national-park day immediately after flying.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport includes the main Wyoming rental-car block estimate.

dailyItinerary.title: Jenny Lake boat, Hidden Falls, and String Lake picnic
dailyItinerary.transport: Jackson to Jenny Lake and String Lake, about 35-45 minutes each way plus park stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Take the Jenny Lake shuttle boat if conditions are good, do the light Hidden Falls version with a carrier, then picnic or wade at String Lake.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If boats/crowds/weather are off, do Taggart Lake trailhead area viewpoints, Mormon Row, and Moose-Wilson Road.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Groceries breakfast, packed picnic lunch, early Jackson dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier for Hidden Falls; stroller only for paved/flat areas. Treat the boat as optional.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check Jenny Lake shuttle season/times and parking pressure before committing.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the original Teton trip's signature day, kept in the expanded version because it is high-payoff without needing a long hike.
moments: Cross Jenny Lake by boat under the peaks.
See Hidden Falls in the lightest realistic version.
Let String Lake be the nap-friendly reset.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity estimate covers boat tickets and park/parking-related incidentals.

dailyItinerary.title: Grand Teton to Old Faithful via West Thumb
dailyItinerary.transport: Drive Jackson to Old Faithful through Grand Teton and Yellowstone South Entrance, about 2.5-3.5 hours before stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Stop at Oxbow Bend or Jackson Lake early, enter Yellowstone, walk West Thumb boardwalk, then settle near Old Faithful.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the drive stretches long, skip West Thumb and use the Old Faithful boardwalk at golden hour.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Jackson groceries breakfast, packed lunch, Old Faithful area cafeteria/lodge dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Break the drive into two nap-friendly legs and avoid late geyser-basin wandering after check-in.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book Yellowstone lodging early and confirm South Entrance/road status before travel.
dailyItinerary.why: This is where the alt version stops being a Teton loop and becomes a true Yellowstone/Teton paired park trip.
moments: Say goodbye to the Teton skyline at Oxbow Bend.
Walk Yellowstone's lake-edge thermal basin without a long hike.
Sleep inside geyser country for the next morning.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Park pass costs are treated as shared activity incidentals across the park days.

dailyItinerary.title: Old Faithful and Upper Geyser Basin boardwalks
dailyItinerary.transport: Mostly walk/shuttle within Old Faithful village.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Old Faithful eruption viewing, Upper Geyser Basin boardwalk in short sections, lodge breaks, and optional Biscuit Basin if parking and baby mood align.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If weather is cold or smoky, use the visitor center, lodge lobby, and only the closest geyser viewing.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Lodge breakfast, picnic/snacks from the room, early lodge dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Boardwalks are stroller-friendly in pieces, but bring the carrier for crowds and stairs.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check current boardwalk closures and Old Faithful prediction windows.
dailyItinerary.why: Sleeping near Old Faithful lets the day be made of short thermal walks rather than hours in the car.
moments: Watch an Old Faithful eruption without rushing from another base.
Dip into the Upper Geyser Basin until the baby is done.
Retreat to the lodge whenever the weather turns.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Most value comes from location; activity cost is low once lodging is secured.

dailyItinerary.title: Grand Prismatic, Norris choice, and transfer to Canyon
dailyItinerary.transport: Old Faithful to Canyon via Midway/Norris, about 1.5-2.5 hours before stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Grand Prismatic overlook if the baby can do the carrier walk; otherwise Midway boardwalk, then Norris Geyser Basin or direct transfer to Canyon.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Skip Grand Prismatic overlook and use Firehole Lake Drive or lodge downtime if parking is rough.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Old Faithful breakfast, picnic lunch, Canyon cafeteria/lodge dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier day. The overlook is optional and should not become a forced march.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm road construction and parking/closure status around Midway and Norris.
dailyItinerary.why: This transfer day gives Yellowstone's most surreal colors a chance without turning it into a marathon.
moments: See Grand Prismatic from the best realistic angle if conditions allow.
Use Norris only if everyone still has bandwidth.
Arrive at Canyon before dinner, not after dark.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Costs are mostly lodging/food because Yellowstone sightseeing is low-ticket once inside the park.

dailyItinerary.title: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone and Hayden Valley
dailyItinerary.transport: Short Canyon-area drives plus Hayden Valley wildlife loop.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Upper/Lower Falls viewpoints, Artist Point, Canyon visitor area, then Hayden Valley from car pullouts around the best wildlife window.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If roads/weather are rough, do Canyon visitor center, Lake Yellowstone lunch, and one close waterfall viewpoint.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Canyon breakfast, picnic/visitor center lunch, Canyon or Lake dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Wildlife stays from the car or safe pullouts. No bison-distance heroics.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check official wildlife safety rules and current road status the night before.
dailyItinerary.why: Canyon plus Hayden Valley is the reason to add the second Yellowstone base rather than only sampling Old Faithful from the Tetons.
moments: Stand at Artist Point for the classic canyon view.
Let wildlife viewing happen from the safety of the car.
Keep the afternoon flexible if the morning is already enough.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Low direct activity cost; the value is lodging location and park access.

dailyItinerary.title: Fly Yellowstone region to Oregon and settle near Bend
dailyItinerary.overnight: Sunriver Resort or SCP Redmond Hotel
dailyItinerary.transport: Exit Yellowstone to JAC, BZN, or BOI depending fare; fly to PDX or RDM; pick up Oregon rental car. Boise bridge is the practical fallback.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: This is a logistics day: airport transfer, flight hop, Oregon car pickup, groceries, and pool/room reset.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If same-day Bend is too much, overnight near PDX or RDM and start Oregon driving Day 9.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Park/airport breakfast, airport lunch, groceries and simple Bend/Sunriver dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Treat the Oregon hop as a second arrival day. No sightseeing requirement.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Compare JAC-PDX/RDM, BZN-PDX/RDM, and BOI-PDX/RDM before locking the car route.
dailyItinerary.why: The flight hop is what makes the expanded version plausible with a one-year-old; driving Yellowstone to Oregon would consume the heart of the trip.
moments: Close the national-park chapter cleanly.
Reset laundry and groceries in Oregon.
Accept that today is about logistics, not scenery.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport includes the flight-positioning placeholder and Oregon rental-car pickup/drop estimate.

dailyItinerary.title: Smith Rock and High Desert Museum
dailyItinerary.overnight: Sunriver Resort or SCP Redmond Hotel
dailyItinerary.transport: Bend/Sunriver to Smith Rock and High Desert Museum, about 1.5-2.5 hours total depending base.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Morning Smith Rock viewpoint/Rim Rock Trail style stroll, then High Desert Museum after nap or as the heat/weather backup.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Skip Smith Rock if hot/smoky and do High Desert Museum, Drake Park, and resort pool.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Resort/condo breakfast, Redmond/Terrebonne lunch, Bend dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Smith Rock is a viewpoint and short-walk day, not a canyon hike day.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check smoke/air quality and High Desert Museum hours.
dailyItinerary.why: After Yellowstone's geysers, Smith Rock gives the trip a high-desert volcanic contrast without a giant hike.
moments: See the Crooked River cliffs from an easy viewpoint.
Use the museum for animals, shade, and structure.
Return to the same Oregon base for naps and laundry.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity estimate covers park pass/parking and museum admissions.

dailyItinerary.title: Newberry volcano, lava lands, and Bend slow afternoon
dailyItinerary.overnight: Sunriver Resort or SCP Redmond Hotel
dailyItinerary.transport: Local Bend/Sunriver driving to Newberry and Lava Lands.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Lava Lands Visitor Center, Newberry viewpoints, and a short stroller/carrier-friendly volcanic stop, then resort pool or Bend river path.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If air quality or weather is poor, swap to High Desert Museum, Bend cafes, and indoor downtime.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Groceries breakfast, Sunriver/Bend lunch, easy dinner near base.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Avoid long exposed lava walks; pick one or two short stops and protect the afternoon nap.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm seasonal visitor center and road hours before going.
dailyItinerary.why: Newberry makes the Oregon chapter feel connected to Crater Lake: volcanoes, lava, lakes, and short interpretive stops.
moments: Introduce the Cascades geology before Crater Lake.
Keep the terrain baby-safe and short.
Give the afternoon back to the pool or river.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Includes recreation pass/parking and small activity buffer.

dailyItinerary.title: Drive to Crater Lake for rim sunset
dailyItinerary.overnight: Crater Lake Lodge or Mazama Village Cabin
dailyItinerary.transport: Bend/Sunriver to Crater Lake, about 2.5-3 hours before stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Drive to Crater Lake, check in, do Rim Village, Sinnott overlook area, and sunset if visibility is good.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the rim is foggy/smoky, use Mazama/Cleetwood area only if safe, or make it a quiet cabin/lodge evening.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Bend/Sunriver breakfast, packed lunch, lodge/Mazama dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: One-night lodge logistics are worth it only if check-in and bedtime stay simple.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book Crater Lake Lodge/Mazama the moment availability opens; confirm seasonal dining and road status.
dailyItinerary.why: Crater Lake is the Oregon equivalent of a signature national-park reveal and earns the cross-state detour.
moments: Get the first blue-water reveal at Rim Village.
Keep the rim walking short and weather-led.
Sleep close enough for a possible morning second look.
dailyItinerary.costNote: One-night park lodging estimate; Mazama cabins may lower this if lodge rooms are expensive or unavailable.

dailyItinerary.title: Crater Lake morning, waterfalls, and Columbia Gorge base
dailyItinerary.overnight: Skamania Lodge or Hood River Hotel
dailyItinerary.transport: Crater Lake to Columbia Gorge/Mount Hood area, about 4.5-5.5 hours plus stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Second Crater Lake viewpoint if clear, then drive north with Toketee Falls or Umpqua stop only if the day is flowing well.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Skip waterfalls and drive directly to the Gorge if the baby needs an easier transfer.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Lodge breakfast, packed or roadside lunch, Hood River/Skamania dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Longest Oregon drive; split with one real stop and let the rest be nap miles.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm the chosen northbound route and road conditions before leaving Crater Lake.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the connective tissue from volcanic lake country to the final river-and-mountain base.
moments: Take a second look at Crater Lake if the morning is clear.
Add one waterfall only if logistics are friendly.
End near the Gorge so the final full day is easy.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transfer-day cost is mainly lodging, car, and food.

dailyItinerary.title: Mount Hood, Trillium Lake, and Columbia Gorge waterfalls
dailyItinerary.overnight: Skamania Lodge or Hood River Hotel
dailyItinerary.transport: Gorge/Mount Hood loop driving, usually 2-3 hours total if kept disciplined.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Choose the weather-best side: Mount Hood and Trillium Lake for mountain reflections, or Multnomah Falls/Waterfall Corridor and Hood River riverfront.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the day is smoky or rainy, do Hood River cafes, Bonneville Fish Hatchery, lodge pool/spa, and one quick waterfall viewpoint.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Hotel breakfast, Hood River lunch, final Oregon dinner near the lodge or waterfront.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Short stroller/carrier stops only; do not stack every waterfall.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check timed-use/parking rules for Waterfall Corridor and Mount Hood road/weather conditions.
dailyItinerary.why: Mount Hood and the Gorge give the trip a polished Oregon finale that is scenic but close enough to PDX for a sane departure.
moments: See Mount Hood reflected at Trillium Lake if skies are clear.
Pick one or two waterfall stops instead of collecting them all.
End with an early final dinner and packed bags.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Includes parking/pass/timed-use buffer and final-dinner bump.

dailyItinerary.title: Drive to PDX and fly home
dailyItinerary.transport: Drive Gorge/Mount Hood base to PDX, return car, fly PDX to ATL.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Departure only; leave a large airport buffer and avoid trying to sightsee in Portland before the flight.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If flight is late, use a simple riverfront or airport-area lunch, but keep bags/car-seat logistics easy.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Hotel breakfast, airport lunch/dinner depending flight time.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Book a late-morning or afternoon flight so the drive and car return are not painful.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Choose PDX departure after 11 am if possible; confirm rental car return location.
dailyItinerary.why: Ending near Portland keeps the final travel day simple after a big multi-destination route.
moments: Keep the last morning practical.
Return the car with time to manage bags and stroller.
Fly home from a larger airport with better schedule options.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Return flight is included in the Day 1 flight placeholder; this day includes airport transport/food only.

routeMap.note: Hybrid route view. Solid/dashed lines are schematic reference legs for the multi-city route; flight hops are intentionally shown as direct reference lines. Numbered day pins may fan out when days share a base.
